blocks.text: Devson Catalyst Ltd makes three families of industrial process consumables at a single site in GIDC Wadhwan, Surendranagar, Gujarat: catalysts (chloride guards, sulphur guards, Claus, hydrotreating and reforming catalysts), adsorbents (molecular sieves, activated alumina) and ceramic media (ceramic/alumina balls and tower packing) [F] (PPT Jul 2026). The products sit inside refinery, petrochemical, gas-processing, fertilizer, steel (DRI) and emission-control units, where they protect downstream catalyst beds, remove impurities or physically support reactor beds [F] (PPT Jul 2026). The company earns money by selling these materials by the tonne against customer purchase orders and tenders; management describes the business as 'tender-based' and 'approval-driven' [MC] (PPT Jul 2026).

Geography: exports to '15+ countries' and presence in 22 Indian states/UTs [MC] (PPT Jul 2026); the screener profile also says 'over 15 countries' [F] (SCREENER). The export share of revenue is not disclosed in the documents available to us.

Customer profile: 79.33% of FY26 revenue came from repeat customers, and repeat customers made up 56.77% of the customer count [MC] (PPT Jul 2026). Top-customer concentration is not disclosed. The only customers named in the available documents are NMDC and Tata Steel, which placed orders for a newly developed ammonia decomposition catalyst on 4 September 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
Scale: FY26 revenue from operations Rs 55.78 cr, EBITDA Rs 16.76 cr, PAT Rs 12.52 cr [F] (PPT Jul 2026); our statements data rounds these to Rs 56 / 17 / 13 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: **Listing status and evidence base.** Devson listed on BSE SME on 16 July 2026 at Rs 118 per share through a Rs 42.34 cr issue that was 203.18x subscribed [F] (PPT Jul 2026). The stock trades at Rs 319 [F] (NUMBERS). The FY26 annual report was filed on 7 September 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) but its text was not available to us. Neither was the prospectus, and as an SME company it has no earnings calls or quarterly results for us to read. This report therefore rests on a July 2026 investor presentation, a short profile, exchange announcement summaries, four years of screener statements and our earlier internal notes. Several standard forensic items (auditor opinion, CARO, related-party transactions, contingent liabilities, customer concentration) are **not disclosed** in what we have, and we treat that absence as a finding in itself.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. **The price implies about 63% annual sales growth for five years**, against a 14.6% base-case equivalent. All three DCF scenarios (bear Rs 42.6, base Rs 74.2, bull Rs 103.8 per share) sit 67-87% below the Rs 319 price [F] (NUMBERS).

2. **Cash conversion is poor.** Over FY24-FY26 operating cash flow was 0.36x reported profit, and cumulative three-year free cash flow was Rs 1 cr [F] (NUMBERS). In FY26 CFO was Rs 4.56 cr against PAT of Rs 12.52 cr [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

3. **The FY26 margin jump coincided with a large inventory build.** The change in finished-goods/WIP/stock-in-trade inventory credited Rs 4.83 cr to FY26 costs, against Rs 0.67 cr in FY25 [F] (PPT Jul 2026). EBITDA rose by Rs 5.83 cr [E] (PPT Jul 2026). The year-on-year increase in that inventory credit, Rs 4.16 cr, equals 71% of the EBITDA increase [E]. Revenue grew only 4.9% [E] (PPT Jul 2026).
4. **Receivables are stretching.** Debtor days went from 57 (FY23) to 110 (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS). Trade receivables rose 32% to Rs 16.75 cr while revenue rose 4.9% [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

5. **Top-line growth has stalled.** FY26 revenue grew 4.9% (company data) or 5.7% (rounded screener data) [E] (PPT Jul 2026; NUMBERS). The product mix swung sharply: adsorbents fell 68% after rising 230% the year before [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

6. **Disclosure is thin and there is no track record.** The company listed on SME on 16 July 2026, reports half-yearly and has 731 shareholders [F] (PPT Jul 2026; NUMBERS). Customer concentration, order book, export share, related-party transactions and the auditor's report are not available in our evidence set [AI].
7. **All production is at one site in Surendranagar, Gujarat** [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Any outage stops all three product lines [AI].

8. **Part of revenue is traded, not manufactured, and traded volumes swing.** Purchases of stock-in-trade were Rs 8.36 cr in FY25 and Rs 2.48 cr in FY26 [F] (PPT Jul 2026), which matches the adsorbent revenue swing [AI].

9. **The share count and the issue split are not reconciled.** Market cap of Rs 434 cr at Rs 319 implies about 1.361 cr shares [F] (NUMBERS). Pre-IPO capital of 1.025 cr shares plus 35.88 lakh offered shares would be about 1.384 cr [E] (PPT Jul 2026). The listed objects total Rs 35.08 cr against a Rs 42.34 cr issue [E] (PPT Jul 2026), so any offer-for-sale component is not disclosed.

blocks.text: [AI] The market seems to be pricing Devson as a scarce Indian catalyst platform that will compound on the back of import substitution. Our reading of the documents is more modest. It is a Rs 56 cr, single-site maker of guard-bed catalysts, adsorbents and ceramic support media. Revenue growth was flat in FY26, and the margin step-up coincided with a Rs 4.83 cr inventory build [F] (PPT Jul 2026). A contrarian bull would argue that none of these models capture the capacity doubling or new products such as the ammonia decomposition catalyst. That argument depends on disclosures (order values, capacity timelines, customer data) that the company has not yet made.

subsections.title: How recent the current business really is

blocks.text: [AI] The legal entity is 22 years old; the 22nd AGM notice in September 2026 is consistent with a 2004 incorporation [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). The business has changed over that time, though: the company started in electrical insulators and moved into catalysts [F] (SCREENER), and the date of that transition is not disclosed. The financial record we can see covers only FY23-FY26. Over that period revenue went from Rs 33 cr to Rs 56 cr and PAT from Rs 2 cr to Rs 13 cr [F] (NUMBERS). The present public-company governance structure (independent directors from 2025, internal and secretarial auditors appointed August 2026) is less than two years old [F] (PPT Jul 2026; ANNOUNCEMENTS). For investors, the listed-company track record is about two months long.

items: Catalysts and adsorbents [F] (PPT Jul 2026): raw material testing -> mixing -> forming -> ageing and drying -> flash calcining -> visual inspection -> calcination -> sizing and sieving -> comprehensive testing -> composite sampling -> packaging -> dispatch.

Ceramic balls [F] (PPT Jul 2026): raw material testing -> pulverizing -> forming -> ageing and drying -> visual inspection -> calcination -> sieving and sorting -> laboratory testing -> packing and dispatch.
Commercial flow [MC] (PPT Jul 2026): vendor approval / prequalification -> technical, commercial and financial assessments -> tender or order -> order-wise approvals -> supply -> ongoing audits.

blocks.text: [AI] Value is captured at qualification and in the thermal processing steps. Once a refinery or fertilizer plant approves a guard-bed or support-media grade, replacement orders tend to go to the approved supplier because switching requires revalidation, which management itself stresses [MC] (PPT Jul 2026). These products usually protect a more expensive main catalyst that licensors supply, so Devson sits in the protective and ancillary layer of the catalyst value chain rather than the high-value reaction catalyst layer. The FY26 gross margin proxy of 51.3% [E] (PPT Jul 2026) shows the pricing power this layer can have in a good year. The 34.0% in FY24 [E] (PPT Jul 2026) shows it is not constant.

Fixed assets were Rs 12 cr against Rs 56 cr of FY26 sales, a fixed-asset turnover of 4.67x (6.14-7.57x in FY24-FY25) [F] (NUMBERS). Cumulative capex over FY24-FY26 was Rs 8 cr [F] (NUMBERS), against a Rs 13 cr increase in sales over the same period [E] (NUMBERS). [AI] On fixed assets alone this is a light-to-moderate capital model. Working capital is the heavier commitment: debtors plus inventory were Rs 24.50 cr at FY26, twice net PPE [E] (PPT Jul 2026). Outsourcing of manufacturing steps is not disclosed; the traded-goods line shows that some products are bought in and resold [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

blocks.text: [AI] Ceramic balls, tower packing and standard activated alumina are closer to engineered commodities: specifications are standard and many suppliers exist, and price competes once a vendor is approved. Guard-bed catalysts (chloride and sulphur guards) and reforming catalysts are more differentiated because performance ties into the customer's process and failures are costly. Hydrotreating catalysts would be the most differentiated line, but nothing in the documents shows Devson's hydrotreating revenue or reference installations. The product-wise table reports only three aggregate families [F] (PPT Jul 2026), so the revenue weight of the differentiated lines cannot be established.

subsections.title: Catalysts: guard beds, reforming and the new ammonia decomposition catalyst

blocks.text: Position in the value chain [AI]: in refinery hydroprocessing, the main reaction catalyst is typically supplied by a technology licensor or global catalyst major. Devson's guard catalysts (chloride, sulphur) sit upstream of that catalyst to protect it, and its Claus catalyst serves sulphur recovery. That is a real but ancillary position. Our earlier internal notes list Clariant, Axens, Haldor Topsoe and BASF as the import incumbents [AI] (BOARD); the company's documents name no competitor.

items: What exists today: Rs 27.93 cr of FY26 catalyst revenue, 50.56% of product revenue [F] (PPT Jul 2026), and shared catalyst/adsorbent capacity of 2,545 MT at 81.01% utilisation [MC] (PPT Jul 2026).

Steel and hydrogen: reforming catalysts are marketed for DRI and ammonia plants [F] (PPT Jul 2026), and the NMDC / Tata Steel orders for an ammonia decomposition catalyst are the first named steel-sector evidence [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
Government / PSU exposure: 'scale advantages in PSU contracts' is claimed [MC] (PPT Jul 2026); NMDC is state-owned [AI]. The PSU share of revenue is not disclosed.

blocks.text: Ceramic balls brought in Rs 21.31 cr in FY26 (38.59%) [F] (PPT Jul 2026). That is either real price and mix improvement or a timing effect between production and sales. [AI] This is the line most clearly constrained by capacity, and therefore the one where expansion capex should convert into revenue fastest. It is also the most commoditised.

[AI] The thesis depends on whether Devson can move from ancillary guard-bed and support-media supply into more technical catalysts (hydrotreating, reforming, ammonia decomposition) with named anchor customers. The September 2026 steel orders are the first public evidence of that move. Until values, volumes and repeat orders are disclosed, the catalyst narrative should be treated as class C-E in the order-quality ladder, not class A-B.

blocks.text: **The price requires about 63% annual sales growth for five years, roughly 11.5x FY26 sales by FY31 [E].** That is more than three times the historical 19.3% CAGR and more than double the bull case's starting rate [F] (NUMBERS). The expanded plant at 100% utilisation supports only about 2x FY26 revenue at FY26 realisations [E] (PPT Jul 2026). Delivering the implied growth would need several further expansions or acquisitions, none of which is disclosed [AI].

[AI] The reverse DCF holds margins at 21%. If the FY26 30% EBITDA margin proved sustainable, the required growth would be lower. Two further points: SME valuations often carry a scarcity and liquidity premium that a DCF ignores, and genuinely new products (ammonia decomposition for steel, hydrogen-linked reforming) could open markets larger than the history suggests. We accept these points, but even the bull case (23% margin, 29% starting growth) values the shares at Rs 103.8 [F] (NUMBERS). The counter-argument narrows the gap without closing it.

subsections.title: What the market may be missing

items: On the downside [AI]: the market may be capitalising the FY26 30% margin, which is about 21% excluding the inventory credit, and ignoring that cash profits are about a third of reported profits.

On the upside [AI]: the ammonia decomposition and reforming catalyst lines could lift realisation per tonne well above the FY26 blended Rs 1.03 lakh [E]. A DCF anchored on historical growth would miss that.

blocks.text: Year-5 (FY31) sales span Rs 76.2 cr (bear), Rs 110.7 cr (base) and Rs 144.6 cr (bull) [F] (NUMBERS). The market price implies roughly 11.5x FY26 sales by FY31 at 63% compound growth [E] (NUMBERS). That is far beyond even the bull case and beyond the full-utilisation revenue of the planned plant [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

At Rs 319 the shares trade above all three modelled values: the bull, base and bear DCF values of Rs 103.8, 74.2 and 42.6 are 67.5%, 76.7% and 86.6% below the price [F] (NUMBERS). [AI] The gap is driven by growth expectations, not by discount-rate choice: the full WACC and terminal-growth grid tops out at Rs 98.5 [F] (NUMBERS). A post-IPO scarcity premium on a thin float, and a narrative built on import substitution and new catalysts, together bridge it.

summary.one_line: Devson Catalyst is a real, low-debt, approval-gated niche maker of guard-bed catalysts, adsorbents and ceramic support media, but its FY26 margin jump leaned on an inventory build, cash conversion is weak, core disclosures are missing, and at Rs 319 every modelled DCF value sits 67-87% below the price and implies about 63% annual sales growth for five years.
